# SPE round 5 plan: invoice extraction

The pasted text lists only the field accuracy rows and not the last requirement ID. So I numbered the new rows from R30 as stand-ins, and I will renumber them after the last ID in `spe/spec/spec.md` before saving.

## Where round 4 left off

- Q hit. I predicted 0.91 and Q measured 0.93.
- R missed. I predicted 0.95 and R measured 0.88. The naive same-as-last-round guess of 0.90 was closer than my prediction.
- R's Why broke. It assumed OCR cleanup only helps. The cleanup tool drops line items on two-column layouts (r04 F9, fix open).
- The stop streak is 0 because round 4 had a miss. No config is at a ceiling.

## Specify

### Proposals from round 4

| Proposal | Decision | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| P1 Skip OCR cleanup on two-column layouts | Adopt it as a new config S. Keep R unchanged as a control. | S changes one thing from R. Keeping R lets the eval show whether the skip removes the F9 loss. |
| P2 Add 15 scanned handwriting invoices | Defer. Logged as an open decision (D-r05-1). | The AP lead has not supplied reference fields for these invoices. Q at 0.93 is not a ceiling. A changed task set would also break comparison with round 4. |
| P3 Drop config P | Adopt. Q becomes the reference config. | P trailed Q on every metric in round 4. Dropping P removes a third of the trial cost. P's earlier numbers stay in the log. |

### Configurations

| Config | Definition | Changes one thing from |
|---|---|---|
| Q | Sonnet 5.5 with the schema-first prompt (reference) | none |
| R | Q plus the OCR cleanup tool, unchanged from round 4 | Q |
| S | R, but the agent skips OCR cleanup when its layout check finds two columns | R |

### Requirement table (round 5)

|---|---|---|---|
| R30 | Config S calls OCR cleanup on every invoice except those its layout check marks as two-column. | r04 F9, proposal P1 | The harness reads S's tool-call log. It finds no cleanup call on any invoice tagged two-column in the fixture, and at least one cleanup call on every other scanned invoice. |
| R31 | Before the run, a committed fixture `spe/evals/fixtures/layout-tags.csv` tags each of the 60 invoices for layout (one or two columns) and scan status (scanned or digital). A code check builds it, and I check it by viewing every first page. The agent under test does not build it. | Decision, needed to measure F9 | Selftest: 60 rows, no blanks, and the count of two-column invoices is reported. |
| R32 | The eval reports line-item recall on two-column invoices per config. | r04 F9 | `line_items.recall_two_column` |
| R33 | The eval reports total accuracy on scanned invoices per config. | r04 "Which Why broke" (R's Why) | `totals.match_scanned` |

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| D-r05-1 | Should the eval add 15 scanned handwriting invoices? | Add them in round 6 once the AP lead supplies references | Leave the set at 60 | Task set, every prediction from round 6 on | User and AP lead | Open. The round 5 default is B for this round only. |

Round 5 defaults:
- P1 runs as a new config S, and R stays as a control. You can override this and replace R with S.
- P3 is adopted, so Q is the reference config.
- Each invoice runs 2 trials per config. Each split cell gets up to 2 extra trials.

## Predict

A cell is a hit when the measured value falls inside its band. The round counts toward the stop streak only if every cell hits.

| Metric | Q | R | S | Same as last round | Grader check | Why |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Field accuracy (all 60) | 0.93 ± 0.03 | 0.88 ± 0.03 | 0.93 ± 0.03 | Q 0.93, R 0.88, S none | `fields.exact_match` | Q and R did not change. S removes the two-column loss, and cleanup has not shown a gain yet, so I centered S on Q. |
| Line-item recall, two-column invoices | 0.95 ± 0.05 | 0.70 ± 0.15 | 0.95 ± 0.05 | Not measured in r04 | `line_items.recall_two_column` | F9 says cleanup drops these items. S skips cleanup on them, so S should match Q. |
| Total accuracy, scanned invoices | 0.85 ± 0.08 | 0.90 ± 0.08 | 0.90 ± 0.08 | Not measured in r04 | `totals.match_scanned` | This row tests R's broken r04 claim directly. If R does not beat Q here, cleanup adds nothing and S has no purpose. |

The control regrade computes the round 4 values for the two new slice metrics. Those values go in the log beside the prediction. The saved prediction is not edited.

## Evaluate

### Harness steps and gates (`spe/evals/harness/r05-workflow.js`)

1. **Layout fixture gate.** Build and check `layout-tags.csv` as R31 describes. If fewer than 5 invoices are two-column, the log marks the two-column slice as low power.
2. **Grader selftest.** The AP lead reference fields must score 1.0 on all three checks. Empty output must score 0. Fields shuffled across invoices must fail. If any of these goes wrong, halt.
3. **Control regrade.** Regrade the stored round 4 outputs for Q and R with the round 5 grader. Field accuracy must reproduce 0.93 and 0.88 within 0.005. If it does not, halt and report a grader change.
4. **Dry run.** Run Q, R, and S on one two-column scanned invoice (3 cells). Check that the output matches the schema and that S's log shows cleanup skipped. Check that the peek scan runs.
5. **Launch** the Workflow.

### Workflow rules

- The script holds the round in one `ROUND = 5` constant. No prompt text contains a hand-written round number.
- The trial output schema has vendor, invoice_number, date (ISO), line_items (description, qty, unit_price, amount), total, and po_mismatch flags.
- Code checks run first. A judge runs only when line-item descriptions differ and the code fuzzy match scores below its threshold.
- Trials have no read access to graders, reference fields, predictions, or `spe/`. A scan checks each transcript for those paths and voids any trial that read them.
- The run ends with a failure analysis and a completeness critic.

### Workflow arguments

```json
{
  "ROUND": 5,
  "configs": ["Q", "R", "S"],
  "model": "pinned Sonnet 5.5 id from round 4",
  "tasks": "same 60 invoices as round 4",
  "trials_per_cell": 2,
  "split_cell_extra_trials_max": 2,
  "extra_trials_cap": 60,
  "token_cap": 7000000,
  "ocr_tool_call_cap": 600,
  "on_cap": "skip the trial and log it"
}
```

### Cost estimate (unmeasured)

- The base run is 60 invoices × 3 configs × 2 trials = 360 trials, plus up to 60 extra trials.
- I assume about 10k input tokens and 1.5k output tokens per trial. R and S add about 3k tokens for the OCR tool calls.
- That comes to about 5M tokens before judge calls. Dropping P saves about 2.5M tokens compared with running four configs.
- Before launch I will convert this to dollars with the current Sonnet 5.5 price list. The token cap is the hard stop.

## After approval, in order

1. Save "go again" and the pasted text, word for word, to `spe/spec/transcripts/2026-10-21-r05.md`. Add the round 5 table to `spe/spec/spec.md` and add D-r05-1 to `spe/spec/disagreements.md`. Commit locally as "spe r05: specify".
2. Copy this plan to `spe/plans/r05.md`. Write `spe/predictions/r05.yaml`, starting with `# Saved before the eval ran. Do not edit after the run.` It has round 5, the date 2026-10-21, the author "Claude, approved by the user in plan mode", configs Q, R, and S, every number with its band and Why, and `same_as_last_round`. It replaces `spe/predictions/r05-draft.yaml` if that file exists. Commit locally as "spe r05: predict".
3. Write the harness and the layout fixture, then run gates 1 to 4 in order. Commit locally as "spe r05: evaluate harness". Launch the Workflow.
4. When the completion notice arrives, close out the round. Update `spe/prediction-log.md` with "Which Why broke" and say whether the naive guess was closer. Add new F-numbers to `spe/failures.md` and set F9's fix status from the result. Add "Proposed for round 6" to the spec, write `spe/predictions/r06-draft.yaml`, and update `spe/README.md`. Commit locally as "spe r05: learn" and tag it `spe-r05`.

All commits stay local. Nothing gets pushed. I will halt and report on a budget cap, a leaked answer key, a broken grader, or a decision only you can make.
critiques: The answer is titled "SPE round 5 plan". It opens with "Where round 4 left off" and then goes into a Specify section that rules on the round 4 proposals. That treats "go again" as a respec at the start of round 5, and nobody named the phase.

The proposals table rules on all three with a reason. P1 is adopted as config S with R kept as a control. P2 is deferred for this round because there are no AP lead references and it would break comparison. P3 is adopted because "P trailed Q on every metric in round 4."

Each requirement has a Source column. R30 and R32 cite "r04 F9". R31 cites "needed to measure F9". R33 cites round 4's "Which Why broke". R34 and R35 cite P3 and the P2 deferral, and both proposals trace to round 4 evidence.

Field accuracy centers Q at 0.93 ± 0.03 and R at 0.88 ± 0.03. Those are round 4's measured values. Every cell has a band. The new slice metrics are marked "Not measured in r04", and the plan says the control regrade will compute their round 4 baselines.

Every prediction row has a Why. The field accuracy row explains Q, R and S. The line-item row cites F9. The totals row frames itself as a test of R's broken claim. Its reason for putting Q at 0.85 is thin, but it does give the cleanup assumption behind it.

Step 2 of "After approval" writes spe/predictions/r05.yaml with a do-not-edit header and commits it as "spe r05: predict". Step 3 builds the harness and launches the Workflow only after that commit. So the prediction is saved and committed before any trial runs.
The harness lists ordered gates before "Launch". They are a layout fixture gate, a grader selftest that halts on failure, a control regrade of round 4 outputs within 0.005, and a 3-cell dry run.
